payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the frog in the toilet bowl visually read as occupying the bowl, rather than as a flat overlay on its interior?
node.criteria: Pass if the bowl frog's overlap or occlusion with the bowl, bowl-relative scale and perspective, and apparent contact make it read as occupying the toilet bowl. Fail if it clearly reads as a flat overlay that does not occupy the bowl. Do not require photorealism or a particular editing technique. Unknown only if the frog's relation to the bowl cannot be judged from the image.
node.source_quote: Put a frog in the toilet
node.endpoint: The frog reads visually as placed within the toilet, not merely overlaid on the bowl interior.
node.necessity: The request specifies putting a frog in the toilet. Assessing the bowl frog's spatial relation distinguishes occupying the toilet from merely appearing over its opening, without adding a style or technique requirement.

node_traces.evidence: Compared with the source, the edited image adds a frog inside the toilet opening. It is sized to the bowl and appears behind the front rim, with parts of its body and feet overlapping the visible interior, so it reads as occupying the bowl rather than lying flat over it.

The source bowl is empty, so this frog was added, but its placement does not visually read as occupying the bowl.

In the edited image, the frog inside the toilet opening is sharply rendered and sits on top of the bowl interior without convincing bowl-relative perspective or occlusion; its feet appear superimposed over the inner surface. The source shows the same bowl opening without a frog.
